title: Introduce probe prioritizer and deferred-alert orchestrator for noisy-smoke suppression
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: CI smoke and periodic probe jobs produce a high volume of low-value failures (transient infra flakiness, tokenization edge-cases, ephemeral model OOMs) that drown actionable regression signals and generate alert fatigue. This change introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a Proportional Failure Prioritizer that assigns a dynamic severity score to eval failures based on recurrence, user-impact heuristics, and cross-cohort hit-rate; and 2) a Deferred-Alert Orchestrator CI hook that applies graded suppression policies (time-windowed backoff, soft-fail routing to triage, and scheduled replays) so only high-confidence regressions surface as Pager notifications. Motivation: reduce noise from transient or low-impact regressions, surface real quality regressions faster, and preserve historical context for later triage. Summary of changes: adds a new prioritizer module (eval_harness/prioritizer.py) and a new CI hook (ci/hooks/deferred_alert_orchestrator.py), updates the runner to annotate failures with a priority key, extends the heartbeat reporter to emit priority histogram metrics, and adds a lightweight replay scheduler that re-executes flagged probes after exponential backoff. Tests and coverage: unit tests for prioritizer heuristics and replay backoff, integration test that exercises the orchestrator with a synthetic failure stream, and a smoke CI job fixture. Compatibility: default behavior is opt-in via the eval-config flag "enable_prioritizer" and the CI job needs to set the new secret/agent token to enable scheduled replays in the central runner. Rollout plan: merged behind a feature flag, staged rollout (alpha teams -> canary -> all), and a 2-week monitoring window with dashboards added to the console. Related work: builds on ENG-1423 (probe-sampling) and links to PM-341 (alert-reduction initiative).
